schwerpunkt: Make the harness learn from what just happened so it doesn't happen again — embed operational learning as permanent capabilities through proposals coherent with the planning brief's 54-decision schema

decisions.decision: Create a command-type Stop hook (shared/hooks/lagebeurteilung-checkpoint.sh) that injects context rot mitigation as context grows past ~20% threshold
decisions.rationale: Instructions at context position 0 lose salience as context grows (Reibung). The commander observed this in real-time: corrections made early in the session were forgotten by later turns. The mitigation must be injected WHERE the rot occurs (mid-context), not where context starts. N-level delegation provides fresh injection at each boundary for subagents; sessions need active injection via Stop hook.
components: (1) New hook: shared/hooks/lagebeurteilung-checkpoint.sh
(2) Event: Stop — fires after every agent turn
(3) Type: command (NOT prompt — needs conditional logic for threshold check)
(4) Threshold heuristic: check transcript file size or turn count as proxy for context growth. Calibrate empirically: ~20% estimated context usage before first injection
(5) Below threshold: silent (exit 0, no output)
(6) Above threshold: emit additionalContext via stderr JSON with Lagebeurteilung reminder

(7) Reminder content: re-read running estimate, audit conversation in reverse chronological order, use ultrathink, check for stale assumptions, surface discrepancies rather than silently resolving them

(8) For delegation (structural, not hook): multi-agent patterns keep subagents short (fresh context at each launch). N-level delegation creates N injection points. This is the delegation-level mitigation — no mid-subagent hook needed because subagents should not grow large enough to rot
(9) PreToolUse on Agent: separate hook reminding S3 to refresh running estimate and verify delegation premise before each launch. Not threshold-gated — fires every delegation.

(10) Operational learning duty injected at END of every delegation prompt (after files loaded, closest to where agent works). Content: observe discrepancies, surface as findings, propose harness improvements, connect to frameworks
(11) Register in tool-ops.json via /tool-ops with verification cases
(12) Deploy to ~/.claude/hooks/ via setup-user-hooks
provenance: Lagebeurteilung (Bundeswehr) — mandatory category walkthrough at fixed intervals, even if nothing changed
Situation awareness theory (Endsley) — SA degradation in long-duration operations, periodic re-orientation required
OODA Orient (Boyd) — re-examine mental model before each decision cycle
Periodic inspection (safety engineering) — scheduled re-verification of system state regardless of observed condition

decisions.decision: Every delegation prompt injects an operational learning duty block — every agent observes, surfaces, proposes, and connects findings to frameworks. This is continuous, not session-end only.
decisions.rationale: The commander stated: 'this should be part of every SESSION and MISSION. operational learning is continuous.' The 40-agent session demonstrated ad-hoc learning (corrections propagated through FRAGORD and relaunch). This decision makes it structural: every agent has the duty, not just the final S2 consolidation.
components: (1) Operational learning duty block: 4-step template (OBSERVE discrepancies, SURFACE as findings, PROPOSE harness improvements, CONNECT to frameworks)
(2) Injected at END of every delegation prompt — after file-reading instructions, closest to where agent works (anti-context-rot positioning)
(3) Every agent AAR includes operational learning section — what did this agent learn that the harness should embed?
(4) Part of delegation duty — component 11 (new): inject operational learning duty
(5) Part of delegation duty — component 12 (new): inject context rot heuristic (for subagents: at end of prompt; for main S3: the Stop hook handles it)
(6) The duty block itself is a candidate for formalization — agents should report whether the duty block helped in their AAR
provenance: Double-loop learning (Argyris) — learning that changes the governing variables, not just the actions
CALL OIL taxonomy (US Army) — observation → insight → lesson-identified → lesson-learned progression
Kaizen (Toyota) — continuous improvement embedded in every operation, not a separate activity
Deming PDCA Check-Act — the learning phases applied continuously, not periodically

decisions.rationale: Unanimous across M1, M2, M4 — every investigation independently identified this as the root cause blocker. The workspace rule, decision #50, and the carry-forward principle all specify tracked paths under .aitools/ that the blanket gitignore defeats. Wave 1 item 3 in the handoff's Schwerpunkt.
components: (1) Remove: .aitools/
(2) Add: .aitools/scratch/
(3) Add: .aitools/channel/session-*/
(4) Add: .aitools/channel/.current-session
(5) Add: .aitools/.current-session
(6) Effect: running-estimate.json, channel/handoffs/, harvesting/ (when migrated), briefings/ all become trackable
(7) M4 verified these patterns are correct for concurrent sessions
(8) Both root AND nested .gitignore strategies needed (root for aitools repo, nested template for other projects)

decisions.decision: Codify 5 multi-agent orchestration patterns from the 40-agent session as part of Mission Command, with PATTERN-CHECK as delegation duty component 10
decisions.rationale: M9 root cause: Mission Command governs individual delegations but not the composition of delegations into workflows. The 5 patterns emerged in the 40-agent session, were never codified, and this session repeated the single-agent-per-mission anti-pattern despite having the exemplar. The patterns serve double duty: coordination mechanism AND context rot mitigation for delegation.
components: (1) Write-verify-amend: S3 writes → Verifier checks → S3 amends. For any S3 output that will be consumed by others.
(2) Parallel S2 investigations: same question decomposed into N concurrent S2 agents with different angles. Synthesis by delegating agent.
(3) S2→S3 chaining: S2 intelligence output feeds S3 execution. S3 reads S2 output, not raw state.
(4) WRITE_BLOCKED relaunch (FRAGORD): if agent fails due to environment, kill and relaunch with corrected briefing.
(5) S2 chain deepening: S2 finding triggers deeper S2 investigation. Automatic deepening when surface investigation reveals complexity.
(6) PATTERN-CHECK: delegation duty component 10 — before launching, S3 asks: which pattern applies? Single agent is the exception, not the default.
(7) Reference file: reference/orchestration-patterns.md with concrete examples from 40-agent session
(8) Amend planning brief decision #3 (Mission Command) or new decision #55
provenance: Auftragstaktik (German) — mission-type orders with delegated execution at multiple levels
MDMP war-gaming (US Army) — parallel course-of-action evaluation
A3 Thinking (Toyota) — single-page constraint prevents sub-mission scope bloat
Catchball (Hoshin Kanri) — bidirectional negotiation between S3 and subagents

decisions.decision: Running estimates are per-session (in session-scoped gitignored dirs) with reconciliation at handoff/session-end into a carry-forward estimate at the fixed tracked path
decisions.rationale: Commander runs concurrent sessions on the same repo. Single-file running estimate has write-collision problem. M4 confirmed .current-session has last-writer-wins race condition. Per-session estimates avoid collision; reconciliation at handoff produces the carry-forward version.
components: (1) Per-session: .aitools/channel/session-<id>/running-estimate.json (gitignored, session-scoped)
(2) Carry-forward: .aitools/channel/running-estimate.json (tracked, fixed path)
(3) Reconciliation algorithm: UNION for arrays, LAST-UPDATED-WINS for scalars, MOST-ADVANCED-STATUS for enums
(4) Reconciliation points: SessionEnd, /handoff step 8, explicit user request
(5) Fix .current-session race by using Claude Code session_id for deterministic dir names (M4 proposal P-3)

decisions.decision: User-level skills use /aitool-* naming prefix to avoid collisions with other harnesses
decisions.rationale: Commander noticed /tool-ops wasn't available in grizzlies/customers repos. User-level skills need unique names. Commander chose /aitool-* over /ait-* for clarity.
components: (1) Prefix: /aitool-* for all user-level deployed skills
(2) Three-tier taxonomy: project-only (no prefix, .claude/skills/), user-level (/aitool-*, ~/.claude/skills/), reference-card (read-only user-level with build-time extracted knowledge)
(3) Reference-card pattern: /aitool-ops as read-only cross-repo tool-ops knowledge
(4) Promote /harvest to user-level (only project skill that's truly portable)
(5) Migration path: rename skill directories, update triggers in rules

decisions.decision: S1 (Administration) is launched via S2→S1 delegation for incident filing, glossary updates, and registry maintenance at session/plan end
decisions.rationale: S1 has never been launched in any session despite being defined in decisions #24-26. The flow S3→S2→S1 (3-level delegation) is the designed administrative pattern. S1 uses backward-chronological user prompt heuristic for intent inference when operating with heuristic bypass.
components: (1) S2 consolidation produces filing briefs (what to file, which skill, format)
(2) S1-glossary: files terms via /glossary skill
(3) S1-incident: files incidents via /incident skill
(4) S1 heuristic bypass: when commander grants permission, S1 reads user prompts backward chronologically, cites commander statements as intent evidence, surfaces uncertainty as FINDING
(5) S1 produces assumptions/changes report (easy to consume)
(6) S3 verifies S1 output (spot-check per delegation duty)

decisions.decision: Dashboard production is S2's duty as part of Operational Learning, named YYYY-MM-DD_session-<prefix>-dashboard.html, stored in tracked location
decisions.rationale: Dashboard production exists as practice (40-agent session, this session's M8) but is ungoverned. No rule, skill, or reference defines it. The dashboard IS an AAR artifact — documents what agents did, produced, and failed. Belongs in Operational Learning framework.
components: (1) Dashboard is S2 consolidation duty — produced alongside session AAR
(2) Naming: YYYY-MM-DD_session-<prefix>-dashboard.html
(3) Location: tracked (harvesting/ currently, .aitools/harvesting/ after migration)
(4) Content: agent metadata, context injected, captured intent, delegation duty compliance, AAR outcomes, convergence themes
(5) V2 dashboards produced for all missions at session end (not just the current batch)
